1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/runtime-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 Runtime prefetching extends the static shell with a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) by invoking the route at prefetch time. Ensuring navigations are instant is the foundation: a route that doesn't navigate instantly without runtime prefetching won't navigate instantly with it either. See [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## The tools 42 43 ### Build the static shell 44 45 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 46 47 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 48 49 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 50 51 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 52 53 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) builds on it, resolving a link's URL data on top. 54 55 ### Tune what `` prefetches 56 57 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `` is effectively free. 58 59 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 60 61 ```tsx 62 63 Checkout 64 65 ``` 66 67 With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click. 68 69 ### Validate instant navigation 70 71 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 72 73 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 74 75 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 76 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 77 78 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 79 cacheComponents: true, 80 experimental: { 81 instantInsights: { 82 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 83 }, 84 }, 85 } 86 87 export default nextConfig 88 ``` 89 90
91 How validation simulates different navigations 92 93 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 94 95 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 96 97 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 98 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 99 100 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 101 102
103 104 ### Test it in CI 105 106 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. This makes navigation between routes in your application feel instant, because by the time a user clicks on a link, the data to render the next route is already available client side. 40 41 Next.js automatically prefetches routes linked with the [`` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) when they enter the user's viewport. 42 43 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 44 import Link from 'next/link' 45 46 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 47 return ( 48 49 50
51 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 52 Blog 53 {/* No prefetching */} 54 Contact 55
56 {children} 57 58 59 ) 60 } 61 ``` 62 63 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 64 import Link from 'next/link' 65 66 export default function Layout({ children }) { 67 return ( 68 69 70
71 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 72 Blog 73 {/* No prefetching */} 74 Contact 75
76 {children} 77 78 79 ) 80 } 81 ``` 82 83 How much of the route is prefetched depends on whether it's static or dynamic: 84 85 - **Static Route**: the full route is prefetched. 86 - **Dynamic Route**: prefetching is skipped, or the route is partially prefetched if [`loading.tsx`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) is present. 87 88 By skipping or partially prefetching dynamic routes, Next.js avoids unnecessary work on the server for routes the users may never visit. Fixed. `app/product/page.tsx:1` is the only file I changed.

## The cause

`ProductPage` was `async` and awaited `getInventory()` at the top level. `getInventory` calls `connection()` (`lib/data.ts:4`), a runtime API. Because that await sat above everything in the tree, the whole page — including the static `<h1>` — was excluded from the prerendered shell, so the navigation blocked on the server until inventory resolved.

Next.js told me this itself. With the original code, dev validation reported:

```
Error: Route "/product": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering.
`fetch(...)` or `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route
from being prerendered, blocking the page load ...
    at getInventory ... at ProductPage
```

## The fix

Pushed the dynamic read down into a Suspense-wrapped `<Inventory>` child. `ProductPage` is no longer `async`, so the title lifts into the static shell while inventory streams into the fallback. Inventory stays uncached — it's random per request and explicitly opts out via `connection()`, so caching it would be wrong; the docs' guidance is to keep fresh data behind `<Suspense>` rather than guess a lifetime.

## Verification

- **Build**: `/product` went from fully dynamic to `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content".
- **Static shell** (`.next/server/app/product.html`): contains `Premium Widget` and `Checking availability`, and *not* the inventory.
- **Streaming order**: title and fallback flush first; `in stock` arrives ~45ms later.
- **Freshness intact**: three requests returned 49, 7, 34.
- **Validation**: clean on the fix. I also temporarily restored the original code to confirm the check actually fires — it did, with the error above — so the clean result isn't a false negative.

Two notes on incidental changes: `next build` applied its own mandatory edits to `tsconfig.json` (`jsx: react-jsx`, added `.next/dev/types`) and created `next-env.d.ts`; `next dev` rewrote `AGENTS.md` to wrap the same instructions in its managed `nextjs-agent-rules` markers. All are framework-generated and would reappear on any build. I deleted the `.next/` build cache since your `.gitignore` doesn't cover it.

One thing I could not verify directly: I tried to inspect the client-navigation prefetch payload over curl, but hand-rolled requests hit a 307→404 because the real router sends router-state headers I'd only be guessing at. Dev validation does simulate client navigations, so it's covered structurally — but if you want an assertion on exactly what a click renders, the `instant()` helper from `@next/playwright` is the tool, and I can add that test.
